members.name: mean_variance_optimal_v1
members.thesis: Markowitz mean-variance optimization can be applied to intraday entry timing by computing rolling expected return (EMA of 1-min returns) and rolling variance (realized variance over 30 bars) for a stock, then entering when the instantaneous Sharpe ratio (expected return / sqrt(variance)) exceeds a t
entry_long: Instant_Sharpe > 2.0 (rolling risk-adjusted return is strongly positive)
Sharpe_Percentile > 0.90 (current Sharpe is in top 10% of recent 2-hour window)
entry_short: Instant_Sharpe < -2.0 (rolling risk-adjusted return is strongly negative)
filters: No entries before 09:30 (need 30 bars for variance) or after 15:10
NIFTY 50 not in extreme move (abs(ROC(NIFTY, 60)) < 100 bps)
weaknesses: Instant Sharpe on 1-min returns is extremely noisy — a single large bar can spike the Sharpe to > 2.0 and the confirmation bar check may not be sufficient to filter noise
Variance computed on 30 1-min returns is statistically unreliable; 30 data points give very wide confidence intervals on the variance estimate
The strategy assumes stationary return distributions within the 30-bar window, which is violated during news events, creating false high-Sharpe signals right before large adverse moves
members.prior_art: Markowitz (1952) mean-variance framework; applied to trade timing rather than portfolio construction; Lo (2002) on time-varying Sharpe ratios; rolling Sharpe used in portfolio analytics but not typica

members.name: rolling_sharpe_adaptive_v1
members.thesis: A strategy's real-time performance (measured by rolling Sharpe ratio of its own recent trades) provides information about whether current market conditions are favorable. By computing a rolling Sharpe ratio over the last 20 trade outcomes and scaling position size proportionally, we ride winning str
entry_long: VWAP_Distance > 5 bps (not just barely above vwap)
Rolling_Trade_Sharpe > -1.0 (not in deep drawdown — don't enter when losing badly)
filters: India VIX < 25; if VIX > 20, cap Size_Multiplier at 1.0
NIFTY 50 direction should agree with trade direction
weaknesses: Rolling Sharpe on 20 trades has very high variance — a single large winner or loser can swing the Sharpe dramatically, causing abrupt position size changes that amplify risk

The adaptive sizing creates a pro-cyclical dynamic: after a winning streak, size increases, so the next loss (which is statistically inevitable) is disproportionately large — can give back streak gains in one trade
Base signal (EMA 9/21 crossover + VWAP) is generic — the adaptive sizing layer cannot compensate for a fundamentally weak entry signal; it only helps during favorable regime clustering
members.prior_art: Kelly criterion for optimal sizing; Tharp's position sizing concepts in 'Trade Your Way to Financial Freedom'; adaptive position sizing discussed in Vince's 'The Leverage Space Trading Model'
